IS : 5756 - 1970 


Indian Standard 

CODE FOR PACKAGING OF CARPETS 

0. FOREWORD 


0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Insti¬ 
tution on 12 October 1970, after the draft finalized by the Textile Floor 
Coverings Sectional Conimiitce had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council. 

0.2 Indian carpets are finding increased overseas markets day by day. 
(Jarpeti worth nearly Rs 1.0 crovc.-^ were "a'ipoi tetl in the year 1969-70 
and the carpet industry has set its export taigei for the Fourth Five- 
Year Plan for Rs 20 rrorcs to be achieved by 1973-74. In order to 
ensure that carpets reach ihtir destination in sound condition, 
proper packaging with suitable p.acking mnierials is essential. This 
rode gives details of packaging of carpels wiiicU ensure adequate, pro¬ 
tection to The contents ol the package.^, for example, rolR and bales, 
against possible damage due to the normal handling during transit. 


1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down the procedure of packaging of carpets, 
hand-made or tufted, in the form of roils or bales. 

2. PACKING PjaoefiDURE 

2.1 In ease Xht fcarpets are not mothproofed, the carpets shall be sprin¬ 
kled uniformly with sufficient quantity of insecticides before packing 
chetn in rolls or bales. 

2.1.1 For packing carpets in roll forms, roll the carpets widthwise 
w ith the face inwards. In case more than one carpet is to be packed 
irt the same roll, these should be rolled one over the other. The weight 
of the roll shall preferably be within 200 kg. 

Not* — In caao of big rolls of carpets, wind them on paper cores of adeqaate 
fvaJl thicknesa and strength. 

2.1.2 For packing carpets in bale form, fold each carpet separately 
to the size of the package and stack the folded carpets one over the 
other. The weight of the bale shall preferably be within 200 kg. 

Not* — The tufted carpets shall not be folded. 


2 



IS : 5756 - 1970 


2.2 PackiDg Materials 


2.2.1 The packages shall be wrapped with the following materials in 
the order indicated below: 


Material 

Number of Layers 

a) For internal trade 


Polyethylene film* 

1 

(40 microns thick¬ 


ness, Min) 


Medium hessianf 

2 

b) For export 


Polyethylene film* 

2 

( 40 microns thick¬ 


ness, Min ) 


Medium hessianf 

2

Innermost 

Second and third 

Innermost and 
second 

Third and fourth 


2.2.2 The packing materials shall be of sufficient size to completely 
cover the package with adequate overlapping. The two layers of 
medium hessian shall be tightly stitched with jute twine with distance 
between the two adjacent stitches not more than 5 cm. 

2.3 Every package shall be provided with ears for lifting it. The ears 
shall be formed in the following manner: 

a) After wrapping the roll or bale with polyethylene film, strong 
strips of hessian (about 15 cm wide, with slight twist) shall be 
tied securely around thcToll or bale at every 1 m distance along 
the length, each strip going once round the package as tightly as 
possible and then securely tied with a reef knot. 

b) Two strips of hessian ( each about 15 cm wide and about 60 cm 
length, with slight twist) shall be passed under each strip tied 
earlier around the package and shall be tied with reef knot in 
such a way that these are located diametrically opposite to each 
other. 

c) The package shall then be wrapped with two layers of hessian 
and the free ends of strips mentioned in (b) above, shall be 
brought out by piercing the two layers of hessian. The holes in 
the hessian layers shall be hemmed to prevent fraying. 


*See IS : 2508-1963 Spoci6cation for low density polyethylene films. 
tPreferably conforming to Type I of 18:2818-1964 Specification for Indian 
hessian. 


3 



IS : 5756 - 1970 
3, MARKING 


3*1 The packages shall be neatly stencilled in indelible ink with the 
following information: 

a) Name of contents; 

b) Gross weight, tare and net weight; 

c) Consignees** name, initials or trade-mark; 

d) Destination; and 

e) The legends * USE NO HOOKS’ and * MADE IN INDIA’.
